chunks: Of the proofs of the Imamate of Ibn Hasan (peace be upon him), in addition to what has been mentioned so far,
is that there is no dispute between the Ummah that a Mahdi will rise in this Ummah, who would fill the earth with justice and equity as it shall be fraught with oppression and inequity.

When we have established that the Mahdi is from the progeny of Husain (peace be upon him) and have invalidated any claimant for this position other than Ibn Hasan (peace be upon him), it is proved that he is the one intended by these narrations.

key_terms.ابْنُ الْحَسَنِ: Ibn al-Hasan (referring to Imam Hasan al-Askari or the lineage of Hasan ibn Ali)

ai.seo_question: How is the identity of the Mahdi linked to the Imamate of Ibn al-Hasan in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi employs a deductive theological argument (burhan) to establish the Imamate of Imam Hasan ibn al-Husayn (al-Mujtaba) by narrowing the field of candidates for the Mahdi. He posits that since the Mahdi is universally agreed to be from the progeny of Husain, and he refutes other claimants, the specific identification of Ibn al-Hasan as the Mahdi serves as definitive proof of his Imamate. This highlights the Shia method of using eschatological consensus to validate hierarchical religious authority.
